---
# The body of a repository's `conclusion` job, the one required check. The
# job itself stays in each repository's own workflow, so the check context
# `conclusion` in the ruleset does not depend on this action.
name: CI conclusion
description: >-
  Fail unless every needed job's result is exactly "success", so a job that
  was skipped, cancelled or never finished cannot pass.

inputs:
  needs:
    description: >-
      The `needs` context as JSON, from toJSON(needs) in a job that runs
      with `if: always()` (see the README).
    required: true

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    # harden-runner monitors Linux runners only.
    - name: Harden the runner
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      uses: step-security/harden-runner@1d88384fd173af6ecb012dfd0264a306b711241a  # v2.22.4
      with:
        egress-policy: audit

    # A matrix with a cancelled leg reports "abandoned", not "cancelled", so
    # the check lists what passes, not what fails.
    - name: Fail if any needed job did not succeed
      shell: bash
      env:
        NEEDS: ${{ inputs.needs }}
      run: |
        echo "$NEEDS"
        if ! jq -e 'all(.[]; .result == "success")' <<<"$NEEDS" >/dev/null; then
          echo "A required job did not succeed." >&2
          exit 1
        fi

# Bazel needs the sources anyway.

    value: ${{ steps.fetch.outputs.seconds }}
description: >-
  Harden the runner, set up Bazel with its caches, make Windows and Linux
  arm64 runners build, and fetch the dependencies with retries.

  disk-cache:

      The disk cache key for setup-bazel, or "false" for no disk cache. Pass a
      key that is unique per job, such as the workflow, OS and workspace.
    required: false
    default: "false"
  cache-save:
    description: >-
      Whether this run may save the Bazel caches. Only the main-branch
      cache-warm job passes true (see the README).
    required: false
    default: "false"

      whitespace. The default reads fetch-targets.txt beside this action;
      it includes the tools each workspace declares. Empty skips the fetch.

      on whitespace, relative to working-directory.
    required: false
    default: ""

    description: The directory of the Bazel workspace the fetch runs in.
    required: false
    default: .

      of the fetch step. The Bazel setup attempts are outside it. Keep it
      below the job's timeout, with time left for the rest of the job.

      uses: step-security/harden-runner@1d88384fd173af6ecb012dfd0264a306b711241a  # v2.22.4
      with:
        egress-policy: audit

    # On Windows the rules' scripts run under the shell toolchain's Bash,
    # MSYS2's on the hosted image. Only there: elsewhere Bazel would run
    # genrule commands with it too.
    - name: Point Bazel at Bash

      shell: bash

        # Self-hosted runners have no bazelisk; with a version set, the
        # action downloads it when it's missing, as `bazel`.

        bazelisk-cache: true
        disk-cache: ${{ inputs.disk-cache }}

        repository-cache: |
          - MODULE.bazel
          - MODULE.bazel.lock
          - pins/*.bzl

    - name: Wait before retrying the Bazel setup
      if: steps.setup_bazel_1.outcome == 'failure'
      shell: bash
      run: sleep 60

    - name: Set up Bazel (attempt 2)
      id: setup_bazel_2
      if: steps.setup_bazel_1.outcome == 'failure'
      uses: bazel-contrib/setup-bazel@f34d6a05eae3c24acab7fa54587492daeaeffdab  # 0.19.2

        # Self-hosted runners have no bazelisk; with a version set, the
        # action downloads it when it's missing, as `bazel`.
        bazelisk-version: 1.30.0
        bazelisk-cache: true
        disk-cache: ${{ inputs.disk-cache }}
        # cache_contract_test checks every copy of this hash list.
        repository-cache: |
          - MODULE.bazel
          - MODULE.bazel.lock
          - pins/*.bzl
        cache-save: ${{ inputs.cache-save }}

    - name: Wait before the last Bazel setup attempt
      if: steps.setup_bazel_2.outcome == 'failure'
      shell: bash
      run: sleep 120

    - name: Set up Bazel (attempt 3)
      if: steps.setup_bazel_2.outcome == 'failure'
      uses: bazel-contrib/setup-bazel@f34d6a05eae3c24acab7fa54587492daeaeffdab  # 0.19.2
      with:
        # Self-hosted runners have no bazelisk; with a version set, the
        # action downloads it when it's missing, as `bazel`.

        bazelisk-cache: true
        disk-cache: ${{ inputs.disk-cache }}
        # cache_contract_test checks every copy of this hash list.

          - MODULE.bazel
          - MODULE.bazel.lock
          - pins/*.bzl
        cache-save: ${{ inputs.cache-save }}

    # runner without its own bazelisk has no `bazelisk` command. Link one next
    # to it, in the directory setup-bazel already put on PATH.

      run: |

          dir="$(dirname "${bazel}")"
          # Git Bash prints the Windows path without .exe.

            cp "${dir}/bazel.exe" "${dir}/bazelisk.exe"
          else
            ln -s "${bazel}" "${dir}/bazelisk"

    # container's CPU quota, and Bazel's own CPU count did not follow the
    # quota either: a 2-CPU container scheduled actions as for 16. So the
    # quota goes to pytest-xdist's `-n auto` (pytest_test passes the variable
    # through) and to Bazel's local CPU resources. mutmut's driver reads the
    # quota itself, so it stays out of every action's cache key. A runner with
    # no quota is left alone. After setup-bazel, which writes the user bazelrc

    # it from source there with maturin, which needs Rust and a C compiler. A
    # runner image may have neither, so the step brings both: Rust's
    # standalone component archives and zig, each checked against a pinned
    # sha256, with zig serving as cc, c++ and ar. Python unpacks zig's .tar.xz
    # because an image may lack xz. cc-rs passes Rust's target triple, which
    # zig can't parse, and rustc passes aarch64's -Wl,--fix-cortex-a53-843419,

    # the only target here. fixture_rules' python_env_repo hands PATH to uv, so nothing

    # exists.

        SHA256_RUST_STD: 32d1ddb44cd49d6497ab6a24f440d4286a20b2667fdf928b876f59c66d13d722
        ZIG_VERSION: 0.17.1
        SHA256_ZIG: a1546d5646eb184437918d6635ca6b762a0e889eac09cef720ee7a1ed3fe7795
      run: |  # zizmor: ignore[github-env]
        root="${RUNNER_TEMP}/rust-toolchain"
        mkdir -p "${root}/dl" "${root}/rust" "${root}/zig" "${root}/cc"
        fetch() {
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "${root}/dl/$3" "$1"
          echo "$2  ${root}/dl/$3" | sha256sum -c --quiet -
        }
        for component in rustc:"${SHA256_RUSTC}" cargo:"${SHA256_CARGO}" rust-std:"${SHA256_RUST_STD}"; do
          name="${component%%:*}-${RUST_VERSION}-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"
          fetch "https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/${name}.tar.gz" "${component#*:}" "${name}.tar.gz"
          tar -xzf "${root}/dl/${name}.tar.gz" -C "${root}/dl"
          bash "${root}/dl/${name}/install.sh" --prefix="${root}/rust" --disable-ldconfig >/dev/null
          rm -rf "${root}/dl/${name}" "${root}/dl/${name}.tar.gz"
        done
        zig_name="zig-aarch64-linux-${ZIG_VERSION}"
        fetch "https://ziglang.org/download/${ZIG_VERSION}/${zig_name}.tar.xz" "${SHA256_ZIG}" "${zig_name}.tar.xz"
        python3 -c 'import sys, tarfile; tarfile.open(sys.argv[1], "r:xz").extractall(sys.argv[2], filter="data")' \
          "${root}/dl/${zig_name}.tar.xz" "${root}/zig"
        rm -f "${root}/dl/${zig_name}.tar.xz"
        for tool in cc c++ ar; do
          printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'args=()' 'for arg in "$@"; do' \
            '  case "${arg}" in --target=* | -Wl,--fix-cortex-a53-843419) ;; *) args+=("${arg}") ;; esac' 'done' \
            "exec '${root}/zig/${zig_name}/zig' ${tool} \"\${args[@]}\"" >"${root}/cc/${tool}"
          chmod +x "${root}/cc/${tool}"
        done
        echo "${root}/rust/bin" >>"${GITHUB_PATH}"
        echo "${root}/cc" >>"${GITHUB_PATH}"

    # Some runfiles paths pass Windows' 260-character limit under the
    # default output root in the runner's profile. The user bazelrc reaches
    # the workspace wherever it is. After setup-bazel, which writes that file
    # too and leaves its last line unterminated, hence the leading newline.
    - name: Shorten Bazel's output root
      if: runner.os == 'Windows'
      shell: bash
      run: printf '\nstartup --output_user_root=C:/b\n' >>"$HOME/.bazelrc"

    # Even under that root, a few paths in the Python runtime's packages
    # pass 260 characters; Python reads them only with long paths enabled.
    - name: Enable long paths
      if: runner.os == 'Windows'
      shell: bash
      run: reg add 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem' //v LongPathsEnabled //t REG_DWORD //d 1 //f

    # Fetching hits go.dev's release list (go_sdk.from_file), PyPI, GitHub
    # and the BCR mirror, which can fail for longer than Bazel's own
    # download retries wait. The fetch retries with pauses of 30 seconds,
    # doubling, until the next pause would pass the retry budget. It then
    # fails with the last URL in the output, so a long outage ends in a
    # failure instead of the job's timeout cancelling it. Only the fetch is
    # retried: a test failure never is.
    - name: Fetch, retrying transient failures
      id: fetch
      if: inputs.targets != ''
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
        TARGETS: ${{ inputs.targets }}
        WORKSPACES: . ${{ inputs.fetch-workspaces }}
        # MSYS Bash turns a leading `//` into `/` in an argument to a native
        # program, which breaks a label such as `//tools:pip_audit`.
        MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL: "*"
      run: bash "${GITHUB_ACTION_PATH}/fetch.sh"

    # setup-bazel's post-if is !cancelled(), even after a failed fetch. Remove
    # the incomplete repository cache so its post step cannot archive it.
    - name: Discard an incomplete warm cache
      if: failure() && inputs.cache-save == 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        cache="$HOME/.cache/bazel-repo"
        if [[ $RUNNER_OS == Windows ]]; then
          case "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" in
            [Dd]:*) cache=D:/_bazel-repo ;;
            *) cache=C:/_bazel-repo ;;
          esac
        fi
        rm -rf -- "$cache"

          echo "$2  ${root}/dl/$3" | sha256sum -c --quiet -
        }
        for component in rustc:"${SHA256_RUSTC}" cargo:"${SHA256_CARGO}" rust-std:"${SHA256_RUST_STD}"; do
          name="${component%%:*}-${RUST_VERSION}-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"
          fetch "https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/${name}.tar.gz" "${component#*:}" "${name}.tar.gz"
          tar -xzf "${root}/dl/${name}.tar.gz" -C "${root}/dl"
          bash "${root}/dl/${name}/install.sh" --prefix="${root}/rust" --disable-ldconfig >/dev/null
          rm -rf "${root}/dl/${name}" "${root}/dl/${name}.tar.gz"
        done
        zig_name="zig-aarch64-linux-${ZIG_VERSION}"
        fetch "https://ziglang.org/download/${ZIG_VERSION}/${zig_name}.tar.xz" "${SHA256_ZIG}" "${zig_name}.tar.xz"
        python3 -c 'import sys, tarfile; tarfile.open(sys.argv[1], "r:xz").extractall(sys.argv[2], filter="data")' \
          "${root}/dl/${zig_name}.tar.xz" "${root}/zig"
        rm -f "${root}/dl/${zig_name}.tar.xz"
        for tool in cc c++ ar; do
          printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'args=()' 'for arg in "$@"; do' \
            '  case "${arg}" in --target=* | -Wl,--fix-cortex-a53-843419) ;; *) args+=("${arg}") ;; esac' 'done' \
            "exec '${root}/zig/${zig_name}/zig' ${tool} \"\${args[@]}\"" >"${root}/cc/${tool}"
          chmod +x "${root}/cc/${tool}"
        done
        echo "${root}/rust/bin" >>"${GITHUB_PATH}"
        echo "${root}/cc" >>"${GITHUB_PATH}"

    # Some runfiles paths pass Windows' 260-character limit under the
    # default output root in the runner's profile. The user bazelrc reaches
    # the workspace wherever it is. After setup-bazel, which writes that file
    # too and leaves its last line unterminated, hence the leading newline.
    - name: Shorten Bazel's output root
      if: runner.os == 'Windows'
      shell: bash
      run: printf '\nstartup --output_user_root=C:/b\n' >>"$HOME/.bazelrc"

    # Even under that root, a few paths in the Python runtime's packages
    # pass 260 characters; Python reads them only with long paths enabled.
    - name: Enable long paths
      if: runner.os == 'Windows'
      shell: bash
      run: reg add 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem' //v LongPathsEnabled //t REG_DWORD //d 1 //f

    # Fetching hits go.dev's release list (go_sdk.from_file), PyPI, GitHub
    # and the BCR mirror, which can fail for longer than Bazel's own
    # download retries wait. The fetch retries with pauses of 30 seconds,
    # doubling, until the next pause would pass the retry budget. It then
    # fails with the last URL in the output, so a long outage ends in a
    # failure instead of the job's timeout cancelling it. Only the fetch is
    # retried: a test failure never is.
    - name: Fetch, retrying transient failures
      id: fetch
      if: inputs.targets != ''
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
        TARGETS: ${{ inputs.targets }}
        WORKSPACES: . ${{ inputs.fetch-workspaces }}
        # MSYS Bash turns a leading `//` into `/` in an argument to a native
        # program, which breaks a label such as `//tools:pip_audit`.
        MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL: "*"
      run: bash "${GITHUB_ACTION_PATH}/fetch.sh"

    # setup-bazel's post-if is !cancelled(), even after a failed fetch. Remove
    # the incomplete repository cache so its post step cannot archive it.
    - name: Discard an incomplete warm cache
      if: failure() && inputs.cache-save == 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        cache="$HOME/.cache/bazel-repo"
        if [[ $RUNNER_OS == Windows ]]; then
          case "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" in
            [Dd]:*) cache=D:/_bazel-repo ;;
            *) cache=C:/_bazel-repo ;;
          esac
        fi
        rm -rf -- "$cache"

.github/workflows/ci.yml.base:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright Tony Burns

---
# Main quality gate. Each gate runs as its own job so the PR status shows
# which one fired, and a final `conclusion` job gives branch protection one
# stable required check. Bazel pins and runs every tool.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Which workspaces a change can affect. Each changed file belongs to the
  # deepest workspace directory that holds it, and anything outside the
  # nested ones belongs to the root (workflows, shared rules and configs
  # included). A workspace runs when it owns a changed file or `deps` names
  # the owner: the ids of the local modules its MODULE.bazel overrides
  # (root's python is a dev dependency, which only root's own tests see).
  # Pushes to main and any other event run every workspace.
  plan:
    name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read  # the pull request's changed files, from the GitHub API
    outputs:
      workspaces: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.workspaces }}
      apple: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.apple }}
      swift: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.swift }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@1d88384fd173af6ecb012dfd0264a306b711241a  # v2.22.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Choose the workspaces to test
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          WORKSPACES: |
            [
              {"id": "root", "dir": ".", "deps": ["python"]},
              {"id": "smoke", "dir": "e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "d2", "dir": "diagrams/d2", "deps": ["root"]},
              {
                "id": "structurizr", "dir": "diagrams/structurizr", "deps": ["root"],
                "os": ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26"]
              },
              {"id": "d2-smoke", "dir": "diagrams/d2/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "d2"]},
              {"id": "go", "dir": "go", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "go-smoke", "dir": "go/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "go"]},
              {"id": "python", "dir": "python", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "python-single", "dir": "python/e2e/single", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "python-workspace", "dir": "python/e2e/workspace", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "ansible", "dir": "ansible", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "ansible-e2e", "dir": "ansible/e2e", "deps": ["root", "python", "ansible"]},
              {"id": "typescript", "dir": "typescript", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "typescript-smoke", "dir": "typescript/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "typescript-bare", "dir": "typescript/e2e/bare", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "cloudflare", "dir": "cloudflare", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "cloudflare-smoke", "dir": "cloudflare/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "cloudflare"]},
              {"id": "playwright", "dir": "playwright", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "playwright-smoke", "dir": "playwright/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "playwright"]},
              {"id": "astro", "dir": "astro", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "astro-smoke", "dir": "astro/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "astro"]},
              {"id": "storybook", "dir": "storybook", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright"]},
              {
                "id": "storybook-smoke",
                "dir": "storybook/e2e/smoke",
                "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright", "storybook"]
              },
              {"id": "tokens", "dir": "tokens", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "tokens-smoke", "dir": "tokens/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright", "tokens"]},
              {"id": "apple-smoke", "dir": "apple/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "swift", "dir": "swift", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "swift-smoke", "dir": "swift/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "swift"]}
            ]
        run: |
          files="${RUNNER_TEMP}/changed"
          if [ "${EVENT}" = pull_request ]; then
            gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR}/files" \
              --jq '.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' >"${files}"
          else
            : >"${files}"
          fi
          # The files API lists at most 3000; past that, test everything.
          count="$(wc -l <"${files}")"
          if [ "${EVENT}" != pull_request ] || [ "${count}" -ge 3000 ]; then
            printf '.github/workflows/ci.yml\n' >"${files}"
          fi
          selected="$(jq -c --rawfile files "${files}" '
            . as $ws
            | ($files | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $paths
            | def owner($p):
                ([$ws[] | select(.dir as $d | $d != "." and ($p | startswith($d + "/")))]
                  | max_by(.dir | length) // {id: "root"}) | .id;
              ($paths | map(owner(.)) | unique) as $owners
            | [$ws[]
                | select(.id as $id | .deps as $deps
                    | $owners | any(. == $id or (. as $o | $deps | index($o) != null)))
                | {id, dir, os: (.os // ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26", "windows-2025"])}]
          ' <<<"${WORKSPACES}")"
          # Apple and Swift workspaces need Xcode, so their smoke consumers have
          # jobs of their own on a GitHub-hosted macOS runner.
          # GitHub fails an empty matrix; Apple or Swift changes keep root checks running.
          matrix="$(jq -c --arg event "${EVENT}" '
            map(select(.id != "apple-smoke" and .id != "swift" and .id != "swift-smoke"))
            | if length == 0 then [{id: "root", dir: ".",
                os: ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26", "windows-2025"]}] else . end
            | [.[] | . as $workspace | .os[] | {os: ., workspace: ($workspace | {id, dir})}]
            | map(select($event != "pull_request" or (.os != "macos-26" and .os != "windows-2025")))
          ' <<<"${selected}")"
          apple="$(jq -r 'any(.[]; .id == "apple-smoke")' <<<"${selected}")"
          swift="$(jq -r 'any(.[]; .id == "swift-smoke")' <<<"${selected}")"
          echo "workspaces=${matrix}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          printf 'apple=%s\nswift=%s\n' "${apple}" "${swift}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          ids="$(jq -r 'map(.id) | join(", ")' <<<"${selected}")"
          echo "Testing: ${ids}" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"

  # One writer per platform, from the root whose module files form the key.
  # An exact immutable cache already contains the complete fetch list.
  cache-warm:
    name: "cache-warm (${{ matrix.os }})"
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request'
          && '["ubuntu-26.04","ubuntu-26.04-arm"]'
          || '["ubuntu-26.04","ubuntu-26.04-arm","macos-26","windows-2025"]') }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # KEY-FORMAT setup-bazel@f34d6a05eae3c24acab7fa54587492daeaeffdab
      # Recheck config.js, index.js, and post.js when this pin changes.
      # cache_contract_test pairs this implementation with that exact pin.
      - name: Compute the repository cache key
        id: key
        env:
          OS: ${{ runner.os }}
          ARCH: ${{ runner.arch }}
          # cache_contract_test checks this against repository-cache lists.
          HASH: ${{ hashFiles('MODULE.bazel', 'MODULE.bazel.lock', 'pins/*.bzl') }}
        run: |
          case "$OS" in
            Linux) platform=linux ;;
            macOS) platform=darwin ;;
            Windows) platform=win32 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$ARCH" in
            X64) arch=x64 ;;
            ARM64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "key=setup-bazel-1-${platform}-${arch}-repository-${HASH}" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The cache toolkit includes paths in its archive version.
          node >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT" <<'JS'
            const os = require("os");
            let path = `${os.homedir()}/.cache/bazel-repo`.replaceAll("\\", "/");
            if (os.platform() === "win32") {
              path = process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE.toLowerCase().startsWith("d:")
                ? "D:/_bazel-repo" : "C:/_bazel-repo";
            }
            console.log(`path=${path}`);
          JS

      - name: Look up the exact repository cache
        id: cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9  # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

      - name: Warm the complete repository cache
        id: warm
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          cache-save: true
          fetch-workspaces: go typescript

      - name: Report fetch time and repository cache size
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          FETCH_SECONDS: ${{ steps.warm.outputs.fetch-seconds }}
        run: |
          # Windows uses <output base>-repo, usually D:/_bazel-repo.
          # Reading the effective option also handles a different drive.
          cache=$(bazelisk info repository_cache)
          size=$(du -sk "$cache" | cut -f1)
          printf 'Fetch: %s seconds\n\nRepository cache: %s KiB\n' "$FETCH_SECONDS" "$size" >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # fixture_rules targets Bazel 9.x only (bazel_compatibility >= 9.0.0, and
  # .bazelversion pins the release), so the matrix varies only the platform
  # and the workspace: one job per pair, on each platform the tool pins cover
  # that GitHub hosts, for the workspaces the plan chose. The root covers
  # this repository's gates (buildifier, the lint tests, the shell checks,
  # the bats suite and the rule families' proofs) and preset.update_test,
  # which fails when preset.bazelrc is stale. The smoke consumer's
  # expect_failure_tests pass only when each proof fails for the stated
  # reason. The nested modules are workspaces of their own, each with its
  # own gates and consumers.
  bazel:
    name: "bazel (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.workspace.id }})"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.workspaces) }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Hardens the runner, sets up Bazel and fetches, with the platform
      # workarounds; see .github/actions/README.md. It follows checkout,
      # which a local action needs.
      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.workspace.id }}
          cache-save: false
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}

      # Prints disk and temp space, so a `tar: Write error` in a test action names its cause.
      - name: Report macOS disk and temp space
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-unset}" || true
          df -h / /System/Volumes/Data "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" "$HOME" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "$HOME/.bazel" "$HOME/.cache" 2>&1 || true
          # cspell:ignore maxfiles maxfilesperproc
          sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxfilesperproc 2>&1 || true
          ulimit -a || true

      - name: Build the Go nogo smoke target
        if: matrix.workspace.id == 'go-smoke'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bazelisk build --config=ci //:nogo_smoke

      - name: Test
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci/test.sh"

      # Prints disk and temp space after the tests, including when they fail.
      - name: Report macOS disk and temp space after the tests
        if: always() && runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-unset}" || true
          df -h / /System/Volumes/Data "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" "$HOME" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "$HOME/.bazel" "$HOME/.cache" 2>&1 || true
          # cspell:ignore maxfiles maxfilesperproc
          sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxfilesperproc 2>&1 || true
          ulimit -a || true

      # govulncheck_test needs the network and gives a different answer as
      # advisories are published, so it is manual and `//...` skips it. The
      # smoke module's proofs of it name a vulnerable version of one module,
      # which no later advisory changes, and run on every platform here. Its
      # own module's scan is the `repo` job's.
      - name: Prove govulncheck
        if: matrix.workspace.id == 'go-smoke'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //:govulncheck_proofs

      # A failed run's test logs, so a failure that does not recur can still
      # be read.
      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.workspace.id }}
          path: |
            ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          # The convenience links are dotfiles, which the action skips by default.
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The Swift and Apple smoke consumer needs Xcode, so pushes run on the
  # GitHub-hosted xcode-27 image. Pull requests use Linux with all steps
  # skipped, so macOS queues do not delay `conclusion`. The image's
  # default Xcode is 27.1, so the job selects 27.2 (build 27B52) and prints
  # `xcodebuild -version` before the build. The job always runs, so that
  # `conclusion` sees a success when the plan skipped the workspace; its
  # steps run only on pushes when the plan chose it.
  apple:
    name: "apple (apple-smoke)"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'ubuntu-26.04' || 'xcode-27' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    env:
      RUN_APPLE: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.apple }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Select Xcode 27.2
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        run: |
          sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
          xcodebuild -version | tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"
          grep -qx 'Build version 27B52' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"

      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-apple-smoke
          cache-save: false
          # The default list names tools of the other workspaces.
          targets: //...
          working-directory: apple/e2e/smoke

      - name: Test
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        working-directory: apple/e2e/smoke
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //...

      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && failure() && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-apple-smoke
          path: |
            apple/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            apple/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The Swift smoke uses the same Xcode image and steps as the Apple smoke.
  swift:
    name: "swift (swift-smoke)"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'ubuntu-26.04' || 'xcode-27' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    env:
      RUN_SWIFT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.swift }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Select Xcode 27.2
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        run: |
          sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
          xcodebuild -version | tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"
          grep -qx 'Build version 27B52' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"

      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-swift-smoke
          cache-save: false
          # The default list names tools of the other workspaces.
          targets: //...
          working-directory: swift/e2e/smoke

      - name: Test
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        working-directory: swift/e2e/smoke
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //...

      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && failure() && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-swift-smoke
          path: |
            swift/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            swift/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # Checks that need Git history or the GitHub API, which no sandboxed test
  # can see, in the shared workflow. The local path is for this repository
  # only; a consumer pins example-org/rules-fixture, see .github/actions/README.md.
  repo:
    name: repo
    permissions:
      contents: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/repo-checks.yml
    with:
      gazelle-dirs: go go/e2e/smoke
      govulncheck-target: //tests/self:govulncheck
      govulncheck-working-directory: go
      go-sdk-checksum-dirs: go go/e2e/smoke
      go-sdk-checksum-workspace: go
      module-dirs: >-
        . ansible astro cloudflare diagrams/d2 diagrams/structurizr go playwright python storybook tokens typescript
      pnpm-audit-dirs: typescript cloudflare astro storybook tokens
      pnpm-audit-workspace: typescript

  # Consumers run the composite actions as `example-org/rules-fixture/...@<sha>`, which
  # GitHub fetches from the source archive, so an `export-ignore` that drops
  # one breaks every consumer while this repository's local-path uses pass.
  # `uses:` can't take an expression, so this checks the archive itself.
  archive:
    name: archive
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@1d88384fd173af6ecb012dfd0264a306b711241a  # v2.22.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Fail if the source archive lacks an action
        run: |
          archived=$(git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -t)
          status=0
          for action in .github/actions/*/action.yml; do
            if ! grep -qxF "$action" <<<"$archived"; then
              echo "::error file=$action::the source archive leaves out $action"
              status=1
            fi
          done
          exit "$status"

  # One stable required check for branch protection. The job stays here, by
  # that name, so the ruleset's required context does not change; the action
  # holds the logic. `if: always()` runs it even when a needed job failed. It
  # passes only when every needed job's result is exactly "success", so a gate
  # that was skipped, cancelled or never finished cannot pass.
  conclusion:
    name: conclusion
    if: always()
    needs: [plan, bazel, apple, swift, repo, archive]
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      # Only the actions, which a local action needs checked out.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: .github/actions

      - name: Fail if any needed job did not succeed
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-conclusion
        with:
          needs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
.github/workflows/ci.yml.head:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright Tony Burns

---
# Main quality gate. Each gate runs as its own job so the PR status shows
# which one fired, and a final `conclusion` job gives branch protection one
# stable required check. Bazel pins and runs every tool.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Which workspaces a change can affect. Each changed file belongs to the
  # deepest workspace directory that holds it, and anything outside the
  # nested ones belongs to the root (workflows, shared rules and configs
  # included). A workspace runs when it owns a changed file or `deps` names
  # the owner: the ids of the local modules its MODULE.bazel overrides
  # (root's python is a dev dependency, which only root's own tests see).
  # Pushes to main and any other event run every workspace.
  plan:
    name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read  # the pull request's changed files, from the GitHub API
    outputs:
      workspaces: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.workspaces }}
      apple: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.apple }}
      swift: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.swift }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@aebdcf6156ab6691adf63218240e476564a1ed4c  # v2.23.0
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Choose the workspaces to test
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          WORKSPACES: |
            [
              {"id": "root", "dir": ".", "deps": ["python"]},
              {"id": "smoke", "dir": "e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "d2", "dir": "diagrams/d2", "deps": ["root"]},
              {
                "id": "structurizr", "dir": "diagrams/structurizr", "deps": ["root"],
                "os": ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26"]
              },
              {"id": "d2-smoke", "dir": "diagrams/d2/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "d2"]},
              {"id": "go", "dir": "go", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "go-smoke", "dir": "go/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "go"]},
              {"id": "python", "dir": "python", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "python-single", "dir": "python/e2e/single", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "python-workspace", "dir": "python/e2e/workspace", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "ansible", "dir": "ansible", "deps": ["root", "python"]},
              {"id": "ansible-e2e", "dir": "ansible/e2e", "deps": ["root", "python", "ansible"]},
              {"id": "typescript", "dir": "typescript", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "typescript-smoke", "dir": "typescript/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "typescript-bare", "dir": "typescript/e2e/bare", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "cloudflare", "dir": "cloudflare", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "cloudflare-smoke", "dir": "cloudflare/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "cloudflare"]},
              {"id": "playwright", "dir": "playwright", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "playwright-smoke", "dir": "playwright/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "playwright"]},
              {"id": "astro", "dir": "astro", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "astro-smoke", "dir": "astro/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "astro"]},
              {"id": "storybook", "dir": "storybook", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright"]},
              {
                "id": "storybook-smoke",
                "dir": "storybook/e2e/smoke",
                "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright", "storybook"]
              },
              {"id": "tokens", "dir": "tokens", "deps": ["root", "typescript"]},
              {"id": "tokens-smoke", "dir": "tokens/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "typescript", "playwright", "tokens"]},
              {"id": "apple-smoke", "dir": "apple/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "swift", "dir": "swift", "deps": ["root"]},
              {"id": "swift-smoke", "dir": "swift/e2e/smoke", "deps": ["root", "swift"]}
            ]
        run: |
          files="${RUNNER_TEMP}/changed"
          if [ "${EVENT}" = pull_request ]; then
            gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR}/files" \
              --jq '.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' >"${files}"
          else
            : >"${files}"
          fi
          # The files API lists at most 3000; past that, test everything.
          count="$(wc -l <"${files}")"
          if [ "${EVENT}" != pull_request ] || [ "${count}" -ge 3000 ]; then
            printf '.github/workflows/ci.yml\n' >"${files}"
          fi
          selected="$(jq -c --rawfile files "${files}" '
            . as $ws
            | ($files | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $paths
            | def owner($p):
                ([$ws[] | select(.dir as $d | $d != "." and ($p | startswith($d + "/")))]
                  | max_by(.dir | length) // {id: "root"}) | .id;
              ($paths | map(owner(.)) | unique) as $owners
            | [$ws[]
                | select(.id as $id | .deps as $deps
                    | $owners | any(. == $id or (. as $o | $deps | index($o) != null)))
                | {id, dir, os: (.os // ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26", "windows-2025"])}]
          ' <<<"${WORKSPACES}")"
          # Apple and Swift workspaces need Xcode, so their smoke consumers have
          # jobs of their own on a GitHub-hosted macOS runner.
          # GitHub fails an empty matrix; Apple or Swift changes keep root checks running.
          matrix="$(jq -c --arg event "${EVENT}" '
            map(select(.id != "apple-smoke" and .id != "swift" and .id != "swift-smoke"))
            | if length == 0 then [{id: "root", dir: ".",
                os: ["ubuntu-26.04", "ubuntu-26.04-arm", "macos-26", "windows-2025"]}] else . end
            | [.[] | . as $workspace | .os[] | {os: ., workspace: ($workspace | {id, dir})}]
            | map(select($event != "pull_request" or (.os != "macos-26" and .os != "windows-2025")))
          ' <<<"${selected}")"
          apple="$(jq -r 'any(.[]; .id == "apple-smoke")' <<<"${selected}")"
          swift="$(jq -r 'any(.[]; .id == "swift-smoke")' <<<"${selected}")"
          echo "workspaces=${matrix}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          printf 'apple=%s\nswift=%s\n' "${apple}" "${swift}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          ids="$(jq -r 'map(.id) | join(", ")' <<<"${selected}")"
          echo "Testing: ${ids}" >>"${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"

  # One writer per platform, from the root whose module files form the key.
  # An exact immutable cache already contains the complete fetch list.
  cache-warm:
    name: "cache-warm (${{ matrix.os }})"
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request'
          && '["ubuntu-26.04","ubuntu-26.04-arm"]'
          || '["ubuntu-26.04","ubuntu-26.04-arm","macos-26","windows-2025"]') }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # KEY-FORMAT setup-bazel@f34d6a05eae3c24acab7fa54587492daeaeffdab
      # Recheck config.js, index.js, and post.js when this pin changes.
      # cache_contract_test pairs this implementation with that exact pin.
      - name: Compute the repository cache key
        id: key
        env:
          OS: ${{ runner.os }}
          ARCH: ${{ runner.arch }}
          # cache_contract_test checks this against repository-cache lists.
          HASH: ${{ hashFiles('MODULE.bazel', 'MODULE.bazel.lock', 'pins/*.bzl') }}
        run: |
          case "$OS" in
            Linux) platform=linux ;;
            macOS) platform=darwin ;;
            Windows) platform=win32 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$ARCH" in
            X64) arch=x64 ;;
            ARM64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "key=setup-bazel-1-${platform}-${arch}-repository-${HASH}" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The cache toolkit includes paths in its archive version.
          node >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT" <<'JS'
            const os = require("os");
            let path = `${os.homedir()}/.cache/bazel-repo`.replaceAll("\\", "/");
            if (os.platform() === "win32") {
              path = process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE.toLowerCase().startsWith("d:")
                ? "D:/_bazel-repo" : "C:/_bazel-repo";
            }
            console.log(`path=${path}`);
          JS

      - name: Look up the exact repository cache
        id: cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9  # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

      - name: Warm the complete repository cache
        id: warm
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          cache-save: true
          fetch-workspaces: go typescript

      - name: Report fetch time and repository cache size
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          FETCH_SECONDS: ${{ steps.warm.outputs.fetch-seconds }}
        run: |
          # Windows uses <output base>-repo, usually D:/_bazel-repo.
          # Reading the effective option also handles a different drive.
          cache=$(bazelisk info repository_cache)
          size=$(du -sk "$cache" | cut -f1)
          printf 'Fetch: %s seconds\n\nRepository cache: %s KiB\n' "$FETCH_SECONDS" "$size" >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # fixture_rules targets Bazel 9.x only (bazel_compatibility >= 9.0.0, and
  # .bazelversion pins the release), so the matrix varies only the platform
  # and the workspace: one job per pair, on each platform the tool pins cover
  # that GitHub hosts, for the workspaces the plan chose. The root covers
  # this repository's gates (buildifier, the lint tests, the shell checks,
  # the bats suite and the rule families' proofs) and preset.update_test,
  # which fails when preset.bazelrc is stale. The smoke consumer's
  # expect_failure_tests pass only when each proof fails for the stated
  # reason. The nested modules are workspaces of their own, each with its
  # own gates and consumers.
  bazel:
    name: "bazel (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.workspace.id }})"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.workspaces) }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Hardens the runner, sets up Bazel and fetches, with the platform
      # workarounds; see .github/actions/README.md. It follows checkout,
      # which a local action needs.
      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.workspace.id }}
          cache-save: false
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}

      # Prints disk and temp space, so a `tar: Write error` in a test action names its cause.
      - name: Report macOS disk and temp space
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-unset}" || true
          df -h / /System/Volumes/Data "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" "$HOME" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "$HOME/.bazel" "$HOME/.cache" 2>&1 || true
          # cspell:ignore maxfiles maxfilesperproc
          sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxfilesperproc 2>&1 || true
          ulimit -a || true

      - name: Build the Go nogo smoke target
        if: matrix.workspace.id == 'go-smoke'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bazelisk build --config=ci //:nogo_smoke

      - name: Test
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci/test.sh"

      # Prints disk and temp space after the tests, including when they fail.
      - name: Report macOS disk and temp space after the tests
        if: always() && runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-unset}" || true
          df -h / /System/Volumes/Data "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" "$HOME" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" 2>&1 || true
          du -sh "$HOME/.bazel" "$HOME/.cache" 2>&1 || true
          # cspell:ignore maxfiles maxfilesperproc
          sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxfilesperproc 2>&1 || true
          ulimit -a || true

      # govulncheck_test needs the network and gives a different answer as
      # advisories are published, so it is manual and `//...` skips it. The
      # smoke module's proofs of it name a vulnerable version of one module,
      # which no later advisory changes, and run on every platform here. Its
      # own module's scan is the `repo` job's.
      - name: Prove govulncheck
        if: matrix.workspace.id == 'go-smoke'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //:govulncheck_proofs

      # A failed run's test logs, so a failure that does not recur can still
      # be read.
      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.workspace.id }}
          path: |
            ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            ${{ matrix.workspace.dir }}/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          # The convenience links are dotfiles, which the action skips by default.
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The Swift and Apple smoke consumer needs Xcode, so pushes run on the
  # GitHub-hosted xcode-27 image. Pull requests use Linux with all steps
  # skipped, so macOS queues do not delay `conclusion`. The image's
  # default Xcode is 27.1, so the job selects 27.2 (build 27B52) and prints
  # `xcodebuild -version` before the build. The job always runs, so that
  # `conclusion` sees a success when the plan skipped the workspace; its
  # steps run only on pushes when the plan chose it.
  apple:
    name: "apple (apple-smoke)"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'ubuntu-26.04' || 'xcode-27' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    env:
      RUN_APPLE: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.apple }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Select Xcode 27.2
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        run: |
          sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
          xcodebuild -version | tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"
          grep -qx 'Build version 27B52' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"

      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-apple-smoke
          cache-save: false
          # The default list names tools of the other workspaces.
          targets: //...
          working-directory: apple/e2e/smoke

      - name: Test
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        working-directory: apple/e2e/smoke
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //...

      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && failure() && env.RUN_APPLE == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-apple-smoke
          path: |
            apple/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            apple/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The Swift smoke uses the same Xcode image and steps as the Apple smoke.
  swift:
    name: "swift (swift-smoke)"
    needs: [plan]
    runs-on: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'ubuntu-26.04' || 'xcode-27' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    env:
      RUN_SWIFT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.swift }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Select Xcode 27.2
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        run: |
          sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
          xcodebuild -version | tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"
          grep -qx 'Build version 27B52' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/xcodebuild-version"

      - name: Set up Bazel for CI
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci
        with:
          disk-cache: ${{ github.workflow }}-swift-smoke
          cache-save: false
          # The default list names tools of the other workspaces.
          targets: //...
          working-directory: swift/e2e/smoke

      - name: Test
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        working-directory: swift/e2e/smoke
        run: bazelisk test --config=ci //...

      - name: Keep the test logs
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && failure() && env.RUN_SWIFT == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: testlogs-swift-smoke
          path: |
            swift/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.log
            swift/e2e/smoke/.bazel-testlogs/**/test.xml
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # Checks that need Git history or the GitHub API, which no sandboxed test
  # can see, in the shared workflow. The local path is for this repository
  # only; a consumer pins example-org/rules-fixture, see .github/actions/README.md.
  repo:
    name: repo
    permissions:
      contents: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/repo-checks.yml
    with:
      gazelle-dirs: go go/e2e/smoke
      govulncheck-target: //tests/self:govulncheck
      govulncheck-working-directory: go
      go-sdk-checksum-dirs: go go/e2e/smoke
      go-sdk-checksum-workspace: go
      module-dirs: >-
        . ansible astro cloudflare diagrams/d2 diagrams/structurizr go playwright python storybook tokens typescript
      pnpm-audit-dirs: typescript cloudflare astro storybook tokens
      pnpm-audit-workspace: typescript

  # Consumers run the composite actions as `example-org/rules-fixture/...@<sha>`, which
  # GitHub fetches from the source archive, so an `export-ignore` that drops
  # one breaks every consumer while this repository's local-path uses pass.
  # `uses:` can't take an expression, so this checks the archive itself.
  archive:
    name: archive
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@aebdcf6156ab6691adf63218240e476564a1ed4c  # v2.23.0
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Fail if the source archive lacks an action
        run: |
          archived=$(git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -t)
          status=0
          for action in .github/actions/*/action.yml; do
            if ! grep -qxF "$action" <<<"$archived"; then
              echo "::error file=$action::the source archive leaves out $action"
              status=1
            fi
          done
          exit "$status"

  # One stable required check for branch protection. The job stays here, by
  # that name, so the ruleset's required context does not change; the action
  # holds the logic. `if: always()` runs it even when a needed job failed. It
  # passes only when every needed job's result is exactly "success", so a gate
  # that was skipped, cancelled or never finished cannot pass.
  conclusion:
    name: conclusion
    if: always()
    needs: [plan, bazel, apple, swift, repo, archive]
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      # Only the actions, which a local action needs checked out.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: .github/actions

      - name: Fail if any needed job did not succeed
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-conclusion
        with:
          needs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

.github/workflows/pr-text.yml.base:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

---
# Scans a pull request's title and body for secrets after an edit. The
# `repo` job of repo-checks.yml scans them on every push, under the required
# `conclusion` check; an edit alone starts no CI run, so this workflow scans
# the edited text. Its check isn't required. A repository calls it from its
# own workflow on `pull_request` with `types: [edited]`, and this repository
# runs it on its own pull requests through the `pull_request` trigger.
#
# It sets up Bazel itself, for the reason repo-checks.yml gives.
name: pr-text

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [edited]
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runs-on:

# workflow, so they are inputs here.

# Bazel setup. A retry that would sleep past it fails the step with the URL
# that kept failing, so a long outage ends in a failure instead of the
# job's timeout cancelling it. Keep the budget below `timeout-minutes`
# minus the time of the other steps: //repo/tests:retry_budget_test checks
# the defaults.
#
# A checkout that stalls idles until the job times out and leaves no trace,
# so each attempt gets one minute, where the median is one second. The first
# attempt may fail; a diagnostics step then prints the git version, the runner
# and the network state, and one more attempt follows. A second stall fails
# the job after about two minutes. Both attempts trace git, with the
# Authorization header redacted.
#

# action. A local `./` path in a called workflow resolves in the *caller's*
# checkout, which does not hold that action, and a pinned remote reference
# cannot name the commit that adds it. The repository checks need none of
# that action's Windows or arm64 steps.

  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runs-on:
        description: >-
          The runner label. Unset, a private caller uses the org's private
          runner label and a public caller uses the hosted one.
        type: string
      timeout-minutes:
        description: The job's timeout.
        type: number
        default: 15
      retry-budget-minutes:
        description: >-
          Whole minutes that the gazelle build and `bazel mod tidy` retries
          may spend, all directories together. The Bazel setup attempts
          are outside it. Keep it below `timeout-minutes`, with time left for
          the other steps.
        type: number
        default: 8
      pip-audit-target:
        description: >-
          The Bazel target that audits the locked Python dependencies. Empty
          skips the audit.
        type: string
        default: //tools:pip_audit
      pnpm-audit-dirs:
        description: >-
          Directories, relative to the root and split on whitespace, whose
          pnpm lock `//:pnpm_audit` audits. Empty skips the audit.
        type: string
        default: ""

        description: >-

        type: string
        default: .

        type: string
        default: ""

        default: .

            bazel="$(command -v bazel)"
            dir="$(dirname "${bazel}")"
            # Git Bash prints the Windows path without .exe.
            if [ -f "${dir}/bazel.exe" ]; then
              cp "${dir}/bazel.exe" "${dir}/bazelisk.exe"
            else
              ln -s "${bazel}" "${dir}/bazelisk"
            fi
          fi

      # The caller's checkout lacks this action. Locate the list and script
      # in its Bazel-pinned rules module; Renovate updates that module pin.
      # Only cache-warm saves, so these fetches never publish partial caches.
      - name: Fetch the shared CI tools
        env:
          BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
          DEADLINE: ${{ steps.retry_clock.outputs.deadline }}
          TARGETS: "@default"
          FETCH_ALL: "false"
          WORKSPACES: >-
            . ${{ inputs.gazelle-dirs }} ${{ inputs.pnpm-audit-workspace }}
            ${{ inputs.govulncheck-working-directory }}
        run: |
          location=$(bazelisk query --output=location @fixture_rules//:.github/actions/setup-bazel-ci/fetch-targets.txt)
          manifest=${location%%:[0-9]*}
          bash "$(dirname "$manifest")/fetch.sh"

      # The manifest runs the actionlint runner-label check in both modes.
      - name: Run repository checks without a commit range
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: bazelisk run @fixture_rules//lint:repo_checks -- --no-range

      # The Go workspaces' BUILD files, as gazelle would write them.
      - name: Check that gazelle has nothing to change
        if: inputs.gazelle-dirs != ''
        env:
          BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
          DEADLINE: ${{ steps.retry_clock.outputs.deadline }}
          DIRS: ${{ inputs.gazelle-dirs }}
        run: |
          read -ra dirs <<<"${DIRS}"
          source "${RUNNER_TEMP}/retry.sh"
          for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
            # Build gazelle first, retrying: that is where the downloads
            # happen. The diff run itself exits non-zero when gazelle has
            # changes, a real failure that a retry must not hide.
            retry "${dir}" bazelisk build //:gazelle
            (cd "${dir}" && bazelisk run //:gazelle -- -mode=diff)
          done

      # Each module's MODULE.bazel, as `bazel mod tidy` would write it.
      - name: Check that MODULE.bazel is tidy
        if: inputs.module-dirs != ''
        env:
          BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
          DEADLINE: ${{ steps.retry_clock.outputs.deadline }}
          DIRS: ${{ inputs.module-dirs }}
        run: |
          read -ra dirs <<<"${DIRS}"
          source "${RUNNER_TEMP}/retry.sh"
          files=()
          for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
            # mod tidy downloads a helper binary from GitHub, so retry it. The
            # diff below is the real check and runs once.
            retry "${dir}" bazelisk mod tidy
            files+=("${dir}/MODULE.bazel")
          done
          git diff --exit-code -- "${files[@]}"

      # The scans download the gitleaks binary from GitHub releases, which
      # can fail like the downloads above. Build their targets first, under
      # the shared deadline. The scans below run once: a finding is real and
      # a retry must not hide it.
      - name: Fetch gitleaks, retrying transient failures
        env:
          BUDGET: ${{ inputs.retry-budget-minutes }}
          DEADLINE: ${{ steps.retry_clock.outputs.deadline }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          source "${RUNNER_TEMP}/retry.sh"
          retry . bazelisk build //:gitleaks_history
          if [[ ${EVENT} == pull_request ]]; then
            retry . bazelisk build @fixture_rules//lint:gitleaks_text
          fi

      # Git history is not a declared input, so the history scan runs
      # outside the test graph; //:gitleaks_test covers the working tree.
      # Pull requests scan HEAD^1..HEAD, the merge commit and the PR's own
      # commits. The checkout step pins no ref, so HEAD is the merge ref on
      # pull_request; EXPECTED_HEAD is the backstop if that ever changes.
      # Changes to .gitleaks.toml or .gitleaksignore, or unexpected Git state,
      # require the full checked-out history, so tightened rules meet old history.
      # The private config (GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML) changes out of band; those
      # changes surface on the next full scan (push to main), the same accepted
      # limit as a rules version bump.
      # Every other event scans the full checked-out history with HEAD.
      - name: Scan Git history for secrets
        env:
          EXPECTED_HEAD: ${{ github.sha }}
          GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML: ${{ secrets.GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML }}
          SCAN_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '--merge-range' || '--log-opts=HEAD' }}
        run: bazelisk run //:gitleaks_history -- "$SCAN_MODE"

      # A pull request's title becomes the merge commit's title and its body
      # is public with it, so both get the same rules as the history.
      # pr-text.yml scans them again after an edit.
      - name: Scan the pull request's title and body for secrets
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML: ${{ secrets.GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML }}
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z ${PR_TITLE} ]]; then
            echo "The pull request event carries no title to scan." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          text="${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr-text.txt"
          printf '%s\n\n%s\n' "${PR_TITLE}" "${PR_BODY}" >"${text}"
          bazelisk run @fixture_rules//lint:gitleaks_text <"${text}"

      - name: Run the local repository checks
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}^{commit}" || git fetch origin "${BASE_SHA}"
          # A live read for the baseline exemption; a failed read leaves it
          # empty and the exemption off.
          MAIN_TIP=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/branches/main" --jq .commit.sha 2>/dev/null) || MAIN_TIP=
          export MAIN_TIP PR_AUTHOR GH_TOKEN REPO PR_BASE_SHA="${BASE_SHA}"
          bazelisk run @fixture_rules//lint:repo_checks -- --base-branch "${BASE_REF}" "${HEAD_SHA}" "${HEAD_BRANCH}"

      # Advisories change without any input changing, so the audit is never
      # a cached test. External index failures must not block pull requests.
      - name: Audit the locked Python dependencies
        if: inputs.pip-audit-target != ''
        continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ inputs.pip-audit-target }}
        run: bazelisk run "${TARGET}"

      # The same for each pnpm toolchain lock.
      - name: Audit the locked pnpm toolchains
        if: inputs.pnpm-audit-dirs != ''
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.pnpm-audit-workspace }}
        env:
          DIRS: ${{ inputs.pnpm-audit-dirs }}
        run: |
          read -ra dirs <<<"${DIRS}"
          for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
            bazelisk run //:pnpm_audit -- --dir "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/${dir}"
          done

      # The Go code, against the vulnerability database, the same way. The
      # SARIF is kept as an artifact, below, for a failure too.
      - name: Scan Go code for reachable vulnerabilities
        if: inputs.govulncheck-target != ''
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.govulncheck-working-directory }}
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ inputs.govulncheck-target }}
        run: bazelisk run "${TARGET}" -- --sarif="${RUNNER_TEMP}/govulncheck.sarif"

      - name: Keep the govulncheck SARIF
        if: always() && inputs.govulncheck-target != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: govulncheck-sarif
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/govulncheck.sarif
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # This command compares SDK records with the base revision before
      # contacting go.dev. Unrelated module edits skip the network entirely.
      - name: Check changed Go SDK archive checksums
        if: >-
          inputs.go-sdk-checksum-dirs != '' &&
          (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'push')
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.go-sdk-checksum-workspace }}
        env:
          DIRS: ${{ inputs.go-sdk-checksum-dirs }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          read -ra dirs <<<"${DIRS}"
          paths=()
          for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
            paths+=("${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/${dir}")
          done
          bazelisk run @fixture_rules_go//tools:go_sdk_checksums -- \
            --changed-since="${BASE_SHA:?missing change base}" "${paths[@]}"

      # //:zizmor_test runs the offline audits; a token turns on the online
      # ones, which need the network.
      - name: Audit workflow security online
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: >-
          bazelisk run @fixture_rules//lint:zizmor --
          --persona pedantic --no-progress "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.github"

      # //:codeowners_test checks that every pattern matches a path; owner
      # and syntax validation needs GitHub's API. Self-hosted runners may
      # lack gh, so the call uses curl.
      - name: Check CODEOWNERS owners and syntax
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
        run: bazelisk run @fixture_rules//lint:codeowners_errors
